lesson_text: Volume-weighted average price is the benchmark institutions use for execution. Stocks holding above session VWAP are being accumulated; below VWAP they're being distributed. Best long entries on pullbacks to VWAP that hold; best short entries on rejections of VWAP from below. AVWAP from an earnings event or breakout pivot is even more powerful, it marks the price level where smart money started buying.

answer_json.answer: Spread and slippage on small caps

lesson_text: On sub-$2B market cap names with <500k average daily volume, slippage on market orders can eat 0.5-1.5% per round-trip. Use limit orders for entries; use marketable limits (limit 0.5% through best bid/offer) for exits when speed matters. Account for slippage in your reward-to-risk math, a setup with 2R reward on small caps is closer to 1.5R real.

answer_json.answer: Options dealer flow and gamma squeezes

lesson_text: When stocks have heavy call open interest at a price just above current, market makers are short gamma, they must buy more stock as price rises to stay hedged. This amplifies moves above large call strikes. Watch for max-pain levels and key strike clusters in front-month options on stocks that have run sharply. Pin risk near OPEX (3rd Friday) is real.

answer_json.answer: Trading is a probabilistic game, not a certainty game

lesson_text: No setup is 100%. The edge is in: positive expectancy (avg_win × win_rate > avg_loss × loss_rate), large sample sizes (50+ trades per setup before judging), consistent process. Single trades are noise; quarterly results are signal. Focus on executing your plan, not on the outcome of any single trade.

lesson_text: There's no rule that says good analysis must be rewarded, or that trends must continue because they 'should'. The market only rewards traders who adapt to what IS, not what should be. Be willing to be wrong, be quick to cut, and never marry a thesis. Conviction is for losers; flexibility is for survivors.
